note: vulgata.info (MediaWiki), Allioli-Arndt German Bible (1830-34, rev. 1914). No robots.txt exists on the host (a request for it returns a plain HTTP 404 page, not a robots ruleset), so the project's own floor of 2.0s/request applies by default -- see CLAUDE.md 'Scraping vatican.va', extended here to any source with no stated policy. Chapter text lives directly on the 'Kategorie:BIBLIA SACRA:{AT|NT}:{Book}{NN}' category pages themselves (categorymembers is empty for all of them -- these are used as content pages, not true categories), each holding a two-column wikitable: Latin (Clementine) then German (Allioli-Arndt) with per-chapter footnotes below. action=raw and action=render were compared on 9 chapters across narrative, poetic and NT books; none used MediaWiki templates ({{...}}), so action=raw (wikitext) is captured alone as the complete, higher-fidelity source -- action=render adds only HTML wrapping with no additional information. Also captures: the edition's own front/index pages (main portal, AT and NT tables of contents, the general 'Die Heilige Schrift Gottes Wort' introduction), the 59 per-book introduction essays (authorship/date/content) linked from the AT/NT index pages, and the two 'Original Text' title-page scans linked from the main portal. Two anomalous but real (non-redirect) duplicate chapter pages exist -- 'NT:Thes03' (content-identical to 'NT:2Thes03') and 'AT:Sirs48' (near-identical to 'AT:JSir48', minor byte differences) -- both captured under their own titles since they are genuine distinct wiki pages. A parallel family of '<Book>-Vulgata' main-namespace pages exists on this wiki (e.g. 'Chronik-Vulgata') with DIFFERENT introduction text from the pages captured here; they are not linked from this edition's own AT/NT index and were left uncaptured as out of scope for the Allioli-Arndt edition -- flagged for a decision before parsing, not silently dropped. The wider vulgata.info wiki also hosts an unrelated saints/calendar corpus (feast-day pages, main namespace) -- deliberately not captured here.
